title: Cline
summary: A coding-agent candidate for users who want to choose the model provider.

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: IDE extension, CLI and desktop coding agent

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Cline's Terms of Service, last modified 2025-09-25, say extension telemetry and usage data (described as non-code metadata such as click events and generalized usage patterns) is on by default and can be disabled in extension settings; Cline says disabling it stops future telemetry transmission and retention by Cline. The Terms add that when a user has no Cline account and routes all model calls through infrastructure they control, no User Content is collected with Telemetry Data. Cline's Privacy Notice, last updated 2025-09-24, distinguishes model routing: with the user's own API key, content goes directly to the third-party model provider and Cline says it does not collect that content; with Cline-provided API keys, Cline collects User Content to facilitate requests to providers, whose terms and privacy notices govern. An older 2025-02-26 Cline telemetry blog describes telemetry as opt-in, which conflicts with the later-dated Terms. The installed client version, actual settings and payload, pre-disable retention, provider terms and legal suitability were not inspected.

facts.label: Local model inference
facts.value: Yes — documented Ollama and LM Studio options; hardware and model suitability require evaluation.

facts.label: Provider configuration
facts.value: Provider sign-in and bring-your-own-key configurations are documented.

facts.label: MCP support
facts.value: Cline documents MCP servers for connecting external tools and data, with local stdio and remote server configuration paths.

prices.name: Provider usage
prices.billing: Depends on provider and authentication route

sections.heading: Make provider choice explicit
paragraphs: List the configured model provider, the owner of its credentials and the spending controls. Changing the client does not itself change the provider’s data policy. If using a local model, inspect external tools and plugins as separate network boundaries.

sections.heading: Evaluate local-model suitability
paragraphs: Use a representative change and measure whether the chosen model produces an acceptable diff on your hardware. Documented local-runtime support is not proof of sufficient model capability or a fully offline workflow in every configuration.

pros.text: Cline documents local STDIO and remote server configuration, with Streamable HTTP marked as recommended.
MCP server management is documented in both the IDE extension and CLI.

cons.text: SSE is marked legacy; the documented configuration defaults to legacy SSE when the transport type is omitted.
Cline's security guidance says to install trusted servers, limit auto-approval to safe tools, and review calls before approval.
Cline's later-dated Terms say extension telemetry is on by default, while an older Cline blog describes it as opt-in; verify the current installed version and setting.

faqs.question: How does Cline distinguish local and remote MCP servers?
faqs.answer: Local servers use STDIO command and argument configuration; remote servers use a URL. Streamable HTTP is recommended and SSE is legacy.

faqs.question: What MCP approval precautions does Cline document?
faqs.answer: The guidance says to use trusted servers, store secrets in environment variables, limit autoApprove to safe tools, and review tool calls before approval.

faqs.question: When does Cline receive prompts or code, and what does it say about telemetry?
faqs.answer: Cline's Privacy Notice distinguishes BYOK, where it says content goes directly to the provider and is not collected by Cline, from Cline-provided keys, where Cline collects content to facilitate provider requests. Its later-dated Terms say extension telemetry is on by default, while an older blog says opt-in. Check the installed version and settings; the selected provider's terms remain separate.

verdict: Shortlist Cline when model/provider choice is a requirement and you can manage its cost and access controls. Local inference needs a separate capability trial.
bestFor: Developers evaluating provider choice or local models
notFor: Buyers equating a local client with no external data transfer
migration: Preserve repository instructions and rotate provider credentials where appropriate. Check each configured provider and tool independently when changing clients.
gaps: Confirm the installed Cline version and telemetry setting; the later-dated Terms say telemetry is on by default, while the older 2025-02-26 blog says opt-in. No client configuration or payload was inspected.

Confirm the selected model-provider privacy, retention, training and jurisdiction terms; Cline's public BYOK and Cline-provided API-key descriptions do not establish a specific provider or account configuration.
Confirm the applicable Cline account and enterprise terms and legal suitability for the intended use.
